Q: Volatile Variable Coherence A:

Simplicio: So what's the point of volatile then? Salviati: volatile tells the compiler the the "variable" actually is a hardware register. Writes to it may affect things outside of the program, and reads from it may reflect state from outside the program. The compiler must not optimize away any reads or writes. On the other hand, volatile does not require the system to enforce any guarantees about what will happen if the same "variable" is concurrently accessed by two or more CPUs.

Q: iOS EAS Build Fails – “Distribution certificate hasn’t been imported successfully” A:

The instructions below have been tested on Linux and Windows with a successful Expo EAS App Store submission. In short, there are two major issues to get them to accept it:

  1. Apple needs their Apple Intermediate Certificate in the signing chain. In my case I used the Worldwide Developer Relations - G3 (Expiring 02/20/2030 00:00:00 UTC) in the chain to ensure trust has not been violated. I used G3 although other newer ones may work.

  2. For whatever reason legacy mode must be used as their system seems to be setup that way.

Commands:

# Convert Apple WWDR cert (DER → PEM)
openssl x509 -inform DER -in AppleWWDRCAG3.cer -out AppleWWDRCAG3.crt

# Generate private key
openssl genrsa -out apple.key 2048

# Generate CSR
# works with powershell/cmd
openssl req -new -key apple.key -out apple.csr -subj "/emailAddress=<email>/CN=<common_name>"
# OR git bash windows
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 openssl req -new -key apple.key -out apple.csr -subj "/emailAddress=<email>/CN=<common_name>"

# 👉 Upload apple.csr to Apple Developer → Certificates → Apple Distribution
# 👉 Download issued certificate which be your distribution.cer

# Convert cert + key + Apple chain → P12, make sure to use legacy
openssl pkcs12 -export -legacy \
  -inkey apple.key \
  -in distribution.cer \
  -certfile AppleWWDRCAG3.crt \
  -out distribution.p12

# NOTE: Any new or replaced distribution certificate requires
# regenerating the provisioning profile.
